title: Ask every supplier at once, and wait for every price

blocks.text: The price-comparison page asks three to five parts suppliers for a quote and shows them side by side. Each supplier's API takes between half a second and two seconds to answer. Two complaints came in: the page takes as long as all the suppliers added together, and now and then it shows a supplier with no price at all, although the supplier's logs show it answered.
Finish `askAll(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/QuoteRound.java`. `askerFor(...)` already builds the thread that asks one supplier and records its price.
When you're done, a round takes about as long as its slowest supplier, and the page never renders before every price is recorded. About six lines.
The tests use suppliers that answer on cue, so they can hold one back and check what `askAll` does in the meantime.

cases.says: every supplier is asked and its price is recorded under its name
all suppliers are being asked at the same time, so the round takes as long as the slowest one
askAll does not return while suppliers are still answering
askAll waits for a supplier that answers after all the others, whichever position it has in the list

origin.section: Results Come Back at join(): Start Every Worker, Then Join Every One

concepts: Results are complete only after join() returns for every worker, and every worker is started before any is joined, so the work takes as long as the slowest one.
